components: a single C engine file c/glm.c (~2,400 lines) plus small headers
the dense core (~17B params: attention, shared experts, embeddings) kept resident in RAM at int4 (~9.9 GB)
the 21,504 routed experts held on disk (~370 GB int4), streamed on demand
a per-layer LRU cache for streamed experts, with an optional pinned hot-store
the OS page cache used as a free second-level cache
an int4 weight container with an int8 MTP (multi-token prediction) speculation head

outputs.text: colibri v1.0 - GLM-5.2 - 744B MoE - int4 - streaming CPU

architecture_facts: GLM-5.2 is a 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only about 40B params per token
colibri keeps only the ~17B dense core in memory and leaves the 21,504 routed experts on disk
for each token it streams in just the experts that token routes to, then caches them per layer with an LRU policy
so the resident footprint is ~9.9 GB and peak RSS is auto-capped near 20 GB, on a machine with about 25 GB of RAM
the whole engine is one portable C file with no BLAS, no Python at runtime, no GPU, and no Docker
cold decode is slow (roughly one word every 10-20 seconds) but MTP speculation adds 2.2-2.8 tokens per forward pass once the cache is warm
surprising_detail: The memory footprint tracks what a single token needs, not the size of the model. At any instant only the handful of experts a token routes to are awake in RAM; the other 700-plus billion parameters sit dormant on disk and are streamed in per layer. That is why a 744B model, ~370 GB on disk, runs in about 25 GB of RAM.
